en: Points of Controversy (Kathāvatthu),
Minor Section (Khuddakaaḍḍhapaṇṇāsaka),
Twenty-first Chapter (Ekavīsatimavagga)
The Discourse on Non-Separation:
Is the worldling not separated from the phenomena belonging to the three realms?
Yes, he is.
The worldling [is bound] by contacts belonging to the three realms … [and so on] … by feelings … perceptions … belonging to the three realms.
By volitions...
by thoughts...
by faiths...
... by means of energies ...
by means of mindfulness ... by means of concentrations ... [and so on] ...
Is it not the case that one is not secluded from the wisdoms pertaining to the three realms?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is an ordinary person not secluded from the kamma pertaining to the three realms?
“Yes.
“Then at the very moment an ordinary person gives a robe, does he at that same moment enter and dwell in the first jhāna … [and so on] … enter and dwell in the base of infinite space?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … at whatever moment an ordinary person gives almsfood … [as before] … gives lodgings … [as before].
When one gives medicinal requisites as support for the sick, at that moment one enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna … one enters and dwells in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception?
One should not say so … [and so on] … .
Is it not to be said that an ordinary person is not dissociated from kamma pertaining to the three realms?
Yes, it is.

Is it to be said that for an ordinary person (*puthujjana*), the karma leading to the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) and the formless realm (*arūpadhātu*) has been fully understood (*pariññāta*)? Certainly not.
Therefore, it follows that the ordinary person is not yet separated from the karmas pertaining to the three realms (*tedhātuka*) … [and so on].
The Discussion on the Unconscious is finished.
